author: Whenever
text:
Hi All. I have a question. I know it may seem a stupid question to the most of you, but I feel it is important to me for a better understanding, thus a better reading of price. So I hope to may have any very appreciated reply.

I am working on reading every single post and page of this great forum, but I am just at the beginning, So I know that the same question and answer may be in several other places of the forum, but I am not there yet. Sorry if I then repeat it. My question is: W H Y???

We all look at S/D. At Decision points and reactions to that. It is a great thing, I love it and I am having good results on demo.

A Decision Point is when the Market decides that Price is too cheap or too expensive. Ok.

Moreover (or as a result of this) suddendly, in a strong move up or down, it happens to be more Sellers than Buyers or viceversa. That causes the move. And that's clear to me too.

What is unclear to me? W H Y do orders remain unfilled??? Sometimes even months!

It may be that I just still think as a practically for the Market unexisting small retail nobody. But if an order cannot be filled, for any reason, and price (let's think now bearish) goes down, I get a requote proposal, but I do not accept it and that's it. There is no order anymore.

Do you then say that institutions would just keep their pending sell orders there for months?

W H Y if they can use the liquidity in hundreds of other speculations ways? Moreover, to me the move down of price IS a selling order. At any single pip level So the orders at base "propose" themselves again and again at lower price, till they find buyers. Why then do we say that big orders are still up there at base?

Even if I am seeing it working well with my eyes, I just NEED to understand WHY I expect Price to fill them at FTB.

And WHY to expect (or better When) that it won't do it and just run through.

Thanks for your patience to anybody wishing to light me up.

Andrea

author: BabyDragonFX
text:
If you look at order flow, price is moving down not up. The yellow line was tested and could not break above it. Therefore the line is resistance and price is telling you it wants to go further down. The line was never broken, it was tested and then failed back down.

This tells you price is still bearish and expectations is not for a New Structure High (NSH) right now but it may make a New Structure Low (NSL) or retest of support.

author: BabyDragonFX
text: Remember, we are like surfers in a massive ocean; we may not always understand the why but we can always see the signal and just like surfers we must be patient and wait for our set. Once we see price doing or meeting expectations, we are then able to catch the correct wave and move in confluence with the market and where it is going.
